ETERNAL.description: NSE-filed actual Q2 FY2027 conference-call transcript, opened and verified on 29 October 2026.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management confirms a more aggressive store-addition target with a higher FY28 run-rate than FY27; most new stores will be in smaller cities where paybacks are performing well.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "On the quick commerce business, the new store addition targets that you've laid out are more aggressive than they have been in the past and imply a higher run rate of store additions in FY28 versus FY27." ... "That's right, Garima. Directionally, we've also mentioned in the letter that the bulk of the expansion of these new stores will be in smaller cities. We do expect that to be the focus from here on, and we are seeing great outcomes in terms of payback on these stores in these markets that we've expanded into in the last few quarters."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal
next_quarter_outlook.location: Transcript pages 2–3 (PDF pages 3–4); analyst question followed by management confirmation

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management explicitly says Blinkit NOV growth should accelerate year-on-year beginning in the December quarter.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "And just to push on that, you're talking about NOV growth pickup starting the December quarter on a YoY basis?" ... "That's right."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal
next_quarter_outlook.location: Transcript page 7 (PDF page 8); analyst clarification confirmed by management

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Accelerating store additions from OND are not expected to reduce margins in the short term; management expects longer-term expansion.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "No, it was a specific comment. What we are saying here is that as we accelerate store addition, which is starting OND, we don't expect that to hit the margins in the short term. Longer term, of course, margins will continue expanding, but we don't expect that there should be a short-term margin reduction on account of accelerated store addition."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management still sees steady-state NOV per store rising toward about ₹11 lakh per day from ₹9 lakh, though rapid store additions may make the quarterly path uneven.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Basis what we know today, yes, we think NOV per day should go up. We gave guidance last time that in steady state it could get to about INR 11 lakh per day per store. We are at INR 9 lakh today. We do think it will go up directionally over time, but there could be some quarters where the growth in the number of stores is lumpy, and therefore it may not be linearly upwards."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Food-delivery margins are expected to stay broadly flat for one to two years as operating leverage is reinvested to expand the market and absolute adjusted EBITDA.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards. That's what the operating principle is. It's hard to project or comment on margin trajectory every quarter but broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.summary: dark.ai is a few months from launch; the base case is a high-gross-margin, largely self-funded business that could reach profitability relatively quickly, while the next 12 months should reveal whether it becomes meaningful.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "As a base case, we think this could be a high gross margin business, which could fund itself largely and get to profitability pretty soon. That's the outlook right now. It's very early." ... "We expect the next 12 months to tell us whether any of this will become meaningful."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

analyst_focus.topic: How aggressive can Blinkit expansion become without hurting returns?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts repeatedly asked about the upgraded FY28 store plan, smaller-city paybacks, capex per store, competitive visibility, NOV per store and whether accelerated additions would pressure margins.

analyst_focus.topic: Where will growth and margins settle across food delivery and Blinkit?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts pressed on December-quarter Blinkit NOV acceleration, the FY29 adjusted-EBITDA target, food-delivery growth, reinvestment and the durability of margin expansion.

key_risks: A faster dark-store rollout can make store productivity and cash deployment uneven across quarters.
Food-delivery operating leverage is being reinvested, keeping percentage margins broadly flat for one to two years.
dark.ai is explicitly a zero-to-one bet that management may discontinue if product-market fit does not emerge.

material_guidance_changes.magnitude: More aggressive target with a higher FY28 addition run-rate than FY27
material_guidance_changes.explicit_statement: Management confirms the analyst's characterization that the new target is more aggressive and says most expansion will be in smaller cities.

evidence.speaker: Garima Mishra and Akshant Goyal
evidence.quote: "Garima Mishra: On the quick commerce business, the new store addition targets that you've laid out are more aggressive than they have been in the past and imply a higher run rate of store additions in FY28 versus FY27. What is giving you this confidence? ... Akshant Goyal: That's right, Garima. Directionally, we've also mentioned in the letter that the bulk of the expansion of these new stores will be in smaller cities."

key_actuals.value: NOV grew 79% year-on-year; current NOV per dark store is about ₹9 lakh per day.
Management described five consecutive quarters of growth acceleration; it did not provide H2 guidance on the call.
Dark-store count was up roughly 50% year-on-year, while orders and NOV per store continued to grow.

SHRIRAMFIN.description: NSE-filed actual Q2 FY2027 conference-call transcript, opened and verified on 29 October 2026.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: FY27 AUM growth expectation is 15%–17%, down from initial 18%, reflecting cautious growth amid weak monsoon and West Asia uncertainty.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Growth, we have been cautious, even though our initial guidance was 18% growth. Looking at the impact of the war situation in West Asia and the weak monsoon, we have been growing a little less than that. The first quarter, our growth was around 15%. In the second quarter, it was 17%. We will be anywhere growing anywhere between these two 15% to 17%. So we are very cautious in our growth."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Umesh Revankar

next_quarter_outlook.summary: NIM may remain elevated for one or two quarters, then move toward 9% medium term and 8.5% long term as capital is deployed.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "The net interest margin is because of th e capital infusion, there is a temporary increase in the NIM. It is likely to remain at this level maybe for another one quarter or two, then slowly coming down. So, in the medium term, it should come to around 9, then maybe in the long term, it will come to around 8.5."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Umesh Revankar

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management describes a temporary 30–40 bps credit-cost increase in some geographies, not a full-year increase; full-year cost could be below 2.3%.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I said there will be temporary increase of 30 to 40 basis point, and not for the full year. So I feel the full year credit cost can be much lower than the 2.3. Temporarily, it may be for this quarter and next quarter."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Umesh Revankar

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts examined rising Stage 2/3 balances and provisioning.
Analysts questioned growth strategy amid lower borrower income and uncertainty.

bank_lender.credit_growth: AUM rose 16.96% YoY and 4.85% sequentially to INR3,29,021.72 crore. FY27 growth expectation is 15%–17%.
bank_lender.disbursements: Q2 disbursements grew 25.71% YoY to INR54,079.02 crore.
bank_lender.nim_outlook: Q2 NIM 9.52%; expected to normalize toward 9% medium term and 8.5% long term.
bank_lender.credit_cost_outlook: Temporary 30–40 bps increase in some geographies; management explicitly says this is not full-year guidance.

key_risks: Weak monsoon and West Asia uncertainty drive caution on growth.
NIM uplift from capital infusion is temporary.
Temporary localized credit-cost pressure may persist into the next quarter.

Looking at the impact of the war situation in West Asia and the weak monsoon, we have been growing a little less than that. The first quarter, our growth was around 15%. In the second quarter, it was 17%. We will be anywhere growing anywhere between these two 15% to 17%. So we are very cautious in our growth."

INFY.description: NSE-filed actual Q2 FY2027 earnings-call transcript; verified exchange attachment.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: FY27 revenue growth guidance is 1%–2% in constant currency; operating margin guidance remains 20%–22%.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Based on our Q2 performance and revised outlook fo r the rest of the year, our revenue growth guidance is 1% to 2% YoY in constant currency terms. Our operating margin guidance remains the same at 20% to 22%."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Salil Parekh

next_quarter_outlook.summary: H2 faces furloughs and fewer working days; guidance spans further uncertainty through environmental improvement.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, as you know, we are entering the seasonally weaker part of the year. There will be furloughs that will impact the H2, there will be lower working day s and all of those implications and all of those impacts. So that will definitely be there. And like always, we do not have one model that leads to guidance. There are always multiple models that leads to mult iple points of the guidance. At the lower end of the guidance, we have baked in higher uncertainty at the upper end of the guidance, we have baked in an improvement in the environment. At this point in time, we cannot really say where we will end up. I mean that is on how things play out."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jayesh Sanghrajka

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts asked about risk to guidance and the effects of H2 seasonality.

key_risks: H2 furloughs and fewer working days constrain seasonal performance; uncertainty can affect the guidance outcome.

material_guidance_changes.magnitude: Lower bound -0.5 percentage point; upper bound -1 percentage point
material_guidance_changes.explicit_statement: Management describes the old range and revised range in the latest transcript.

evidence.speaker: Jayesh Sanghrajka
evidence.quote: "So if you look at our guidance, our our last guidance was 1.5% to 3%. We had clearly called out at 1.5%, we expect even more uncertainty. Our Q2 has been softer and our volume continues to remain softer. We have also seen pricing pressure on the back of competitive intensity and higher ask on productivity. So all that is baked in, in our revised guidance as we look forward. On top of that, as Salil said, some of the sectors, we see softness, Retail, Hi-Tech, where the discretionary is lower than what we are expecting. So all of that is reflected in our guidance on the revenue and which is where it is 1% to 2% now."

PGEL.description: NSE-filed Q1 FY2027 earnings-call transcript; latest qualifying transcript as of 29 October 2026.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management expects better commodity pass-through and aims for about 8% full-year operating margin, while explicitly calling this an aspiration rather than guidance.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "This year, on an overall basis, I'm expecting margins at the operating level, which is basically ex of PLI, ex of any incentive, etcetera, to improve significantly because that pass-through should be there. So on a reported basis, we should be having a slightly better margin than last year. And initially, at the beginning of this year, we had guided that we should be probably close to 8% kind of a margin for the whole year, at least at the operating level, which is this quarter about 7.3%. And we are hopefully going to reach that number on a full year basis."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Pramod Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.summary: The Sri City refrigerator facility targets commercial production in Q4 FY27 and meaningful revenue from FY28.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Secondly, on our refrigerator facility at Sri City in South India, it is progressing well. We are targeting commercial production by quarter 4 of this financial year and with this becoming a meaningful revenue stream for FY '28 onwards. We have also tied up with our anchor customer for this business, and we are already active discussions with other customers also where we are getting some soft commitments from them."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vishal Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management sees 25%–30% growth potential in FY27 and FY28 as new capacity ramps, followed by possible consolidation in FY29.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So even if, say, '27, '28, I don't see any reason why we will not have 25%, 30% growth for us. And even if say for '29, if it is a consolidation year, we don't mind because in that year, we will be actually consolidating our position, getting our operations much more efficient and getting the profitability, which is ROCE, ROE, which is very important for us at a respectable level so that we can have money to invest in the next phase of growth. So that is what is going to be the strategy."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Pramod Gupta

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts tested when copper, aluminium and resin inflation would be recovered through customer pricing.
Questions focused on compressors, refrigerators, washing machines and the utilization of recent capex.

manufacturer.revenue_growth: Q1 consolidated revenue ₹2,034 crore, up 35.2% YoY.
manufacturer.volume_growth: Room AC volumes grew about 20%–22%; ASP increased about 10%–12%.
manufacturer.order_inflow: Not disclosed; management does not report firm order-book numbers.
manufacturer.demand_outlook: Management expects outsourcing share gains and 25%–30% company growth potential in FY27 and FY28.
manufacturer.margin_outlook: Commodity pass-through should improve; about 8% full-year operating margin is an aspiration, not formal guidance.
manufacturer.ebitda_margin: Q1 EBITDA margin 7.7%; operating margin excluding incentives about 7.3%.

key_risks: Commodity inflation and rupee depreciation may delay price pass-through and margin normalization.
Q4 refrigerator production and compressor ramp depend on project execution and customer uptake.
Management explicitly says the 8% margin figure is an aspiration, not guidance.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance increases to 15%–17%; Hotel segment revenue is expected to grow 17%–19%.

Accordingly, we are revising our full year growth guidance upwards to 15% to 17%. And within that, the Hotel segment revenue is expected to grow by 17% to 19%."

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts examined whether the upgraded full-year guidance remained conservative entering a seasonally strong H2.

APLAPOLLO.description: NSE-filed Q2 FY2027 earnings-call transcript; verified exchange attachment.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management says Q3 has started well, expects more than double-digit growth this quarter and in H2, and targets 175,000 tonnes of roofing-product volume in Q3.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "As you saw in Q2, performance in Q3 has also been good so far. We are not seeing any decline anywhere. We are also looking at more than double -digit growth in this quarter and in the second half. As for roofing products, some of our lines got off to a good start in July. So, I think we are targeting roofing product volumes of 175,000 this quarter."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sanjay Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management expects Q3 EBITDA per tonne to exceed ₹6,000 and describes Q3 as better than Q2.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Q3 is much better than this." ... "Q3 will come above 6,000."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sanjay Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management expects steel-plant shutdowns to keep November difficult, followed by normalization from December and a 400,000-tonne monthly volume run-rate.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "If you look at the market, there is a shortage of steel. I do not even have much steel for the loan business. I do not have much steel to adjust with because all the steel plants have had many shutdowns. November is also bad. From December, all the plants will be back on track, and we will achieve strong volumes of 4 lakh tons per month."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sanjay Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.summary: The company retains 20% absolute EBITDA growth guidance for FY27; a recovery in UAE operations could create upside in H2.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we believe this is sustainable now, as we enter in the second half because the contribution is coming from brand APL Apollo products and roofing category again which are high value-added products. And if the UAE operations recover in the second half on stable geopolitical situation, we may do better than our expected 20% EBITDA growth which we are guiding for FY 2027."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Anubhav Gupta

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts tested whether H2 volume growth can recover and whether EBITDA per tonne above ₹6,000 can repeat in Q3.
Questions focused on when disrupted UAE operations could return and how quickly new capacity could translate into volume and EBITDA.

key_risks: November steel availability remains constrained by mill shutdowns.
UAE recovery and export-container normalization depend on geopolitical and logistics conditions outside management's control.
A rebound in lower-margin SG Premium volumes could reduce EBITDA per tonne even while lifting absolute EBITDA.

TATACONSUM.description: NSE-filed Q2 FY2027 earnings-call transcript; verified exchange attachment.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Tea value growth is expected to move ahead of volume from Q3, while calibrated pricing in tea and salt should begin supporting India margins.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "And as we've continued taking graduated price increases, we expect the equation to start turning value greater than volume starting this quarter." ... "India for the quarter, there was a bit of a contraction of the margin, largely on account of the inflationary pressures that we are seeing on tea and salt. Having said that, of course, we have taken calibrated pricing, which should start from quarter 3."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sunil D'Souza and Ashish Goenka
next_quarter_outlook.role: Managing Director and CEO; Group Chief Financial Officer

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management expects year-on-year margin expansion to continue through H2, supported by tea seasonality, salt price increases and the peak season for Capital Foods.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "For Capital Foods, Q3, Q4, our peak festival and offtake season. So, from every angle, we remain quite confident of continuing to deliver margin expansion quarter -on-quarter versus -- when I say quarter -on-quarter, it is -- you would have to take seasonality into account, so it is versus the same quarter last year. So despite the fact that we delivered higher margins in H2 versus H1 last year, we remain confident of continuing to deliver that this year as well."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sunil D'Souza

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Capital Foods and Organic India growth
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management expects a small Q3 catch-up from delayed shipments and maintains 25%–30% growth expectations for Capital Foods and Organic India.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "There will be some uplift because as we catch up that gap, there will be some uplift coming into this quarter. But overall, I would continue to expect 25% to 30% growth that we had guided for Capital Foods and Organic India going forward."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sunil D'Souza

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management expects tea volumes to return to low- to mid-single-digit growth as pricing corrections, seasonality and new launches take effect.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I would say we'll get back to, I would say, low single digits to mid -single-digit volume growth. I shouldn't -- because we are entering -- remember, we've taken the pricing corrections. We are entering season. And by the way, we've had a flurry of launches as well."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sunil D'Souza

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts repeatedly tested when tea, salt and Capital Foods pricing would offset inflation and restore consolidated margin expansion.
Questions focused on whether 25%–30% growth can persist across Capital Foods, Organic India, Sampann and ready-to-drink products.

key_risks: Tea and salt inflation may take time to pass fully through the P&L.
International growth remains exposed to weather and shipping disruption.
The Q3 catch-up from delayed shipments is described as minor rather than a major demand uplift.
